page: Amazon Web Services c7a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by fourth-generation AMD EPYC 9R14 processors running at 3.7 GHz. The instance delivers 64 physical x86_64 cores across 64 dedicated vCPUs with a single thread per core architecture. System memory consists of 128.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, providing a compute-focused 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core. Vector processing instruction support is broad, including AVX-512 foundations such as AVX-512 VNNI and BF16 extensions alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark evaluations show exceptional parallel execution, with top-tier multi-core results in stress-ng (196,253.01) and Geekbench multi-core (22,073.0), as well as a PassMark CPU score of 93,359.17. High compute density is reinforced by strong Clang software compilation throughput (72,495.0) and ray tracing performance (97,810.0). In memory-intensive scenarios, DDR5 delivers cached read bandwidth reaching 9,316.02 GB/sec and uncached read bandwidth of 296.16 GB/sec, supporting Redis SET throughput of 122.32 million operations per second.

The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage and lacks hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating remote Amazon EBS volumes for persistent disk storage. Network capabilities provide a baseline throughput of 25 Gbps. Relative to its hardware class, the server provides high compute-per-dollar efficiency for parallel mathematical operations, continuous integration build farms, distributed batch processing, simulation engines, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c7a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by dedicated 64-core AMD EPYC 9R14 processors clocked at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 128.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, the instance delivers a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core alongside 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It features support for AVX-512 vector extensions, including VNNI and BF16, but provides no integrated local storage or hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the top tier for multi-core compute in stress-ng and Geekbench, Clang compilation, and in-memory key-value operations like Redis. While persistent storage requires attached EBS volumes, the instance delivers strong cost efficiency for compute-dense workloads, including distributed build systems, media encoding, scientific simulations, batch processing pipelines, and CPU-based inference workloads.
